summary: Joannes van der Vliet was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1869–1874) studying under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He was Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1890) and Professor of Latin at Utrecht University (1891–1892).
Joanny Grosset was an Indologist who completed his Licencié-ès-lettres at the University of Lyon and studied under Paul Regnaud (~1885–1895).

Joaquim Heliodoro da Cunha Rivara worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied mathematics, philosophy, and medicine at the University of Coimbra (1824–1836) and served as a teacher and librarian at the Liceu de Évora (~1838–1855).

Jochem Schindler was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Heinz Kronasser and earned his Ph.D. at Würzburg. He taught at Vienna (1972–1974, 1987) and Harvard (Assistant Professor 1974–1976, Professor 1978–1987).

Joe Bransford Wilson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Geshe Gendun Lodro and Geshe Lhundup Sopa, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia (-1984), and served as Associate Professor at UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Queen Mary University of London and the University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).
Joe Currie works in religious studies and Indology. He has held a post and is a PhD candidate at Harvard University (attested 2026).

Joel Bordeaux is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his BA at Georgia State and his MA, MPhil, and PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Stony Brook, Leiden, Utrecht, and Erasmus University Rotterdam (2025).

Joel Peter Brereton is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler in 1971. He held posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (2004; Professor emeritus ~2001).
Joel Tatelman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford (-1996) under the doctoral supervision of Alexis Sanderson.
Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor (教授) at Shuchiin University, attested in 2010 and 2026.

Joerg Tuske works in philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as an Associate Professor in the Philosophy Department at Salisbury University (attested 2013).

Joey Hung works in computational and Buddhist studies, having studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He held posts at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (Professor and Dean, attested 2026).
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a historian and Indologist who studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency University. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (senior lecturer from 1912), and Patna University (University Reader, 1923).
Johan Andreas dèr Mouw was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1883–1887), earning his Ph.D., and studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern in 1883.

Johan Elverskog works in Iranian/Central Asian, Buddhist, and religious studies. He earned a B.A. at UC Berkeley and an M.A. at Indiana University Bloomington, later becoming Dedman Family Distinguished Professor at Southern Methodist University (~2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber and Antonie Rutgers (doctorate, Leiden, 1851–1855) and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University from 1865 to 1903.

Johan Hendrik Gallée was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Litt. Hum. Dr. at Leiden University (1866–1873) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, taught at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem (1872–1879), and served as lektor at Utrecht University (1881–1892).

Johan Hendrik Kern was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1886–1891) and studied under Eduard Sievers and August Leskien. He held professorships at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and Leiden University (1924–1933).
